## Elements of a Good Viz

1. READABILITY!
2. Labled Axes
3. Conveys your message
4. Units
5. Legend (if applicable)

## Good v. Bad: Examples

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pyprojroot import here # this helps us navigate tricky path stuff between local runs and quarto builds

# Load the data using here() with the path from the project root
file_path = here("lectures/data-week10-jessie/diabetes_dataset.csv") # demographics dataset
diabetes = pd.read_csv(file_path, sep=',')

```

```{python}

#group = diabetes.groupby("smoking_status")
plt.figure()
#for name, gr in group:
plt.scatter(diabetes['diet_score'], diabetes['diabetes_risk_score'])
plt.xlabel('diet score')
plt.ylabel('risk score')
plt.title('diet score vs risk score')
plt.savefig('diet-v-risk.png', dpi = 300, bbox_inches = 'tight')
plt.show()
```

## if we try to add color...

```{python}
group = diabetes.groupby("smoking_status")
plt.figure()
for name, gr in group:
    plt.scatter(gr['diet_score'], gr['diabetes_risk_score'])
plt.xlabel('diet score')
plt.ylabel('risk score')
plt.legend()
plt.title('diet score vs risk score by smoking status')


plt.show()
```

## Instead:

- we can select a random sample of the data to model instead
- `data = data.sample(n = 1000, random_state = 10)`

```{python}
data = diabetes.sample(n = 1000, random_state = 10)
group = data.groupby("smoking_status")
plt.figure()
for name, gr in group:
    plt.scatter(gr['diet_score'], gr['diabetes_risk_score'], label=name)
plt.xlabel('diet score')
plt.ylabel('risk score')
plt.legend()
plt.title('diet score vs risk score by smoking status')

plt.show()
```


## Now with colors:
```{python}
data = diabetes.sample(n = 1000, random_state = 10)
colors = {"Never": "tab:cyan", "Current": "tab:pink", "Former": "green"}
color_list = [colors[group] for group in data['smoking_status']]

plt.figure()
plt.scatter(data['diet_score'], data['diabetes_risk_score'], label=name, c = color_list)
plt.xlabel('diet score')
plt.ylabel('risk score')
plt.legend()
plt.title('diet score vs risk score by smoking status')

plt.show()
```
